purpose: Apples-to-apples tok/s for the 3-way comparison. The committed three_way_table tok/s came from DIFFERENT stacks (A=unsloth 122.8, B/C=plain transformers ~37) and are NOT comparable. Here A(bf16) and B/C(int4) are re-measured under the SAME vLLM engine + identical knobs.
weight_independence_note: Throughput depends only on architecture + numeric precision + serving format, NOT on trained weight VALUES. So we benchmark base Qwen3-1.7B in bf16 (= Method A architecture/precision) and the base quantized to the identical torchao int4 tile-packed format (= Method B AND C serving artifact). B and C share the identical int4 format, so their throughput is identical by construction (one 'bc_int4' row represents both).

matched_knobs.note: ignore_eos + min_tokens=max_tokens forces EXACTLY 128 decode tokens per request for both configs (identical decode work). Both run with CUDA graphs (enforce_eager=false).

BC_int4.represents: Method B (INT4 PTQ) AND Method C (INT4 QAT) — identical torchao int4 tile-packed serving format

derived.single_stream_winner: int4 (memory-bandwidth-bound at batch=1; 4x smaller weights -> less to move)
derived.batched_winner: bf16 (compute-bound at batch=128; bf16 tensor-core GEMM outruns int4 dequant+gemm)
derived.takeaway: Weight-only int4 helps single-stream latency and memory footprint (2.5x smaller), but bf16 wins aggregate throughput under heavy batching on A100. Pick int4 for memory/latency-constrained single-stream serving, bf16 for max batched throughput.
